chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Wassha' from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him say: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) fasted until it was said, "He does not break his fast," then he broke his fast until it was said, "He does not fast," then he fasted the fast of David (peace be upon him): one day and one night [or one day and one night he does not fast], then he was taken (died) upon fasting three days of the month, and he said: "They equal the fast of the whole year and they remove the heat of the chest."'
Hammad said: I said, 'What is al-wahar?' He said: 'Al-wahar is the whispering (of the soul/desire).'
Hammad said: I said, 'Which days are they?' He said: 'The first Thursday of the month, and the first Wednesday after the tenth, and the last Thursday of it.'
I said, 'Why did these days become the days that are fasted?' He said: 'Indeed, those before us from the nations, when punishment descended upon one of them, it descended on these fearful days.'

key_terms.الْأَيَّامُ الْمَخُوفَةُ: The fearful days, referring to days of historical divine punishment
key_terms.الْوَحَر: Heat or internal fever, metaphorically referring to the whispering of desires
key_terms.صَوْمَ الدَّهْرِ: The fast of the whole year (a metaphorical equivalence)
key_terms.صَوْمُ دَاوُدَ: The fast of David, a pattern of fasting one day and skipping one day

ai.seo_question: What are the three specific days of the month recommended for fasting in Shia tradition and what is their spiritual significance?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the Prophet’s (saw) transition to the Sunnah of fasting three specific days monthly, mirroring the continuous fast of Prophet Dawud (as) to balance devotion with physical sustainability. Imam al-Sadiq (as) explains that these days—first Thursday, first Wednesday after the tenth, and last Thursday—are chosen because divine punishment historically descended upon previous nations on these dates, making them days of spiritual protection. The term 'wahar' (chest heat) is clarified as internal whispers or distractions, which fasting helps to purify.
